name: Opus Value
strategy: Contrarian value in capitulated quality: Cigna as the cheapest managed-care name with almost no Medicare Advantage exposure, de-rated cash-flow software and search (Alphabet, Adobe, Microsoft) added into the AI-unwind selloff, a smaller integrated-energy sleeve, and about 41% cash to stage further buying.
reassessment_note: Research this week (web search plus Yahoo daily closes): the UNH stop fired on CMS's proposed CRUSH anti-fraud rule (16 Nov), which extrapolates Medicare Advantage chart-audit findings to whole contracts and claws back to payment year 2018 -- an open-ended liability for UNH/HUM/CVS that I will not re-buy before UNH's promised 2027 guide. Cigna sold its MA business in March 2025 and fell only ~3% on the rule (its risk is Warren-style PBM politics, not CRUSH), so I keep it at full size. The GLD stop fired as gold hit a 14-month low on a hawkish Fed and strong dollar; the Gulf-supply leg of the thesis has also faded with Brent back near $92 on an IEA-forecast surplus, so gold stays out and energy stays a modest hedge rather than growing. SPY fell 8.6% in five sessions on an AI-bubble unwind; GOOGL is 32% off its six-month high and well below its 50/100-day averages, ADBE trades near ~10x forward earnings, MSFT is 13% off its high -- that is the capitulation in quality this mandate exists to buy, but with a hawkish Fed I am staging it: gross rises only from roughly half to 59%, keeping 41% cash for a second tranche. Rewriting the book also resets the stops from Monday's fills.

positions.thesis: Cheapest large managed-care/PBM name; fell 8.8% this week mostly in sympathy with the CRUSH Medicare Advantage audit rule, which barely touches Cigna since it sold its MA book in March 2025; Evernorth is ~86% of adjusted revenue. Kept at 18% (largest leg) because the selloff hit it for a risk it does not carry; the 12% stop from the new fill (~$238) caps the PBM-politics tail.

Search and cloud cash machine now 32% below its six-month high ($390 -> $265) after the AI-capex unwind; raised from 7% to 10% as the clearest quality-at-a-discount in the selloff, sized moderately because heavy capex and antitrust weigh on free cash flow.

Still growing revenue and EPS at double digits with heavy buybacks, yet trades near ~10x forward earnings after a further 10% drop this week on AI-disruption fears; raised from 9% to 10% ahead of its December fiscal-Q4 report, with a wide 18% stop because the stock is volatile and the thesis is multi-quarter.

New leg: highest-quality software balance sheet, down 13% from its six-month high to about its 100-day average ($484) in the AI selloff; a starter 7% because it is less de-rated than ADBE/GOOGL, to be added to if the capitulation deepens.

Cash-generative integrated major retained as an inflation/Iran-Hormuz hedge against the tech-heavy legs; trimmed slightly from 10% because Brent has slid to ~$92 on an IEA-forecast Q4 surplus, so the hedge is kept small, not grown.
Second integrated major held at 5% to diversify single-company risk within the energy hedge; flat since entry and still near its 100-day average, so no reason to change the size.
